hero.subtitle: NosoTrack infers who infected whom in near real-time, enabling hospital control teams to stop outbreaks before they escalate.

steps.label: Crisis
steps.headline: Nosocomial outbreaks are deadly, costly and poorly managed.
steps.subtitle: Healthcare-associated infections affect 1 in 10 patients worldwide. Current control measures rely on broad testing and isolation — but stopping an outbreak requires identifying its specific drivers: patient zero, superspreaders, transmission routes, and undetected cases.

steps.label: Failure
steps.headline: Today's case investigation is slow, manual and labour-intensive.
steps.subtitle: Outbreaks unfold in hours. Investigations take weeks. Control teams chase paper trails while the next ward goes down.

steps.label: Integration
steps.headline: Outbreak forensics, end-to-end.
steps.subtitle: Current tools work in silos. Integration unlocks intelligence. NosoTrack fuses three data streams into a unified analytical engine that infers who-infected-whom in real time.

steps.label: Reconstruction
steps.headline: From scattered cases to a single transmission tree.
steps.subtitle: Bayesian inference fuses genomic distance, contact proximity and admission timing into one probabilistic graph: who infected whom, with confidence on every edge.

steps.label: Reporting
steps.headline: Alerts and reports that hospital teams can actually use.
steps.subtitle: Every inferred outbreak surfaces as a typed alert: scope, suspected index case, transmission routes, projected trajectory. Reports compile in one click for the IPC committee.

steps.label: Co-pilot
steps.headline: An IPC co-pilot, embedded in the workflow.
steps.subtitle: A retrieval-augmented agent reads the inferred tree, the latest guidelines and your local IPC protocols, and proposes the next intervention — ward cohorting, screening sweeps, contact-tracing windows.

title: Methods & Software
research.intro: NosoTrack builds on over a decade of research in outbreak forensics, focusing on the integration of epidemiological, genomic and contact data to infer transmission trees. Our team and collaborators have published extensively on methodological advances, including the outbreaker2 R package and the linktree method for inferring transmission patterns between staff and patients. These methods have been applied to real outbreak data, including SARS-CoV-2 nosocomial outbreaks in Switzerland and the UK, MRSA in neonatal intensive care units in the UK, Klebsiella pneumoniae in a Nepali neonatal unit, Acinetobacter baumannii in hospitals in North Carolina, and Ebola outbreaks in the DRC. We are committed to open science, with all software freely available and publications accessible to the public.
research.timelineLabel: Evolution of Outbreak Forensics: Methods & Applications

timeline.fullTitle: Integrating genetic and epidemiological data to determine transmission pathways of foot-and-mouth disease virus
timeline.description: Integrates genetic and epidemiological data using an SEIR model for transmission; assumes complete bottleneck and all cases observed/sampled; inference via maximum likelihood.
timeline.journal: Proceedings of the Royal Society B

timeline.fullTitle: Reconstructing disease outbreaks from genetic data: a graph approach
timeline.description: Reconstructs transmission trees from genetic data using a graph approach; minimizes total genetic distance; no explicit transmission model.

timeline.fullTitle: Genetic data provide evidence for wind-mediated transmission of highly pathogenic avian influenza
timeline.description: Bayesian method using mutations; SEIR transmission model with spatial kernel; single introduction.
timeline.journal: Proceedings of the Royal Society B

timeline.fullTitle: Infectious disease transmission as a forensic problem: who infected whom?
timeline.description: Frames infectious disease transmission as a forensic problem; uses likelihood-based approach to identify who infected whom from epidemiological data; models serial interval and infectious period distributions.
timeline.journal: Journal of the Royal Society Interface

timeline.fullTitle: Bayesian Reconstruction of Disease Outbreaks by Combining Epidemiologic and Genomic Data
timeline.description: Bayesian reconstruction combining epidemiologic and genomic data; SI transmission model; handles multiple introductions and sampled cases.

timeline.fullTitle: Epidemic Reconstruction in a Phylogenetics Framework: Transmission Trees as Partitions of the Node Set
timeline.description: Simultaneous inference in BEAST framework; coalescent process; SEIR model with spatial kernel.

timeline.fullTitle: Extracting transmission networks from phylogeographic data for epidemic and endemic diseases: Ebola virus in Sierra Leone, 2009 H1N1 pandemic influenza and polio in Nigeria
timeline.description: Uses likelihood ratio test for time of most recent common ancestor; Poisson mutation model; no explicit transmission model.

timeline.fullTitle: Genomic Infectious Disease Epidemiology in Partially Sampled and Ongoing Outbreaks
timeline.description: Bayesian method in R package; coalescent process; SI model; handles ongoing outbreaks and proportion of sampled cases.

timeline.fullTitle: Simultaneous inference of phylogenetic and transmission trees in infectious disease outbreaks
timeline.description: Simultaneous inference in R package; coalescent process; SI model; all cases observed but not always sampled.

timeline.fullTitle: outbreaker2: a modular platform for outbreak reconstruction
timeline.description: A modular platform for outbreak forensics; extends outbreaker with a flexible, module-based architecture allowing custom likelihood functions, movement models, and prior distributions; implemented as an R package.

timeline.fullTitle: When are pathogen genome sequences informative of transmission events?
timeline.description: Investigates when pathogen genome sequences are informative of transmission events; quantifies the relationship between genomic diversity, mutation rates, and the ability to resolve transmission links; provides guidance on when genomic data adds value to epidemiological investigation.

timeline.fullTitle: Bayesian inference of transmission chains using timing of symptoms, pathogen genomes and contact data
timeline.description: Bayesian inference of transmission chains combining timing of symptoms, pathogen genomes, and contact data; extends outbreaker2 framework to integrate contact tracing data as an additional source of information for transmission tree reconstruction.

timeline.fullTitle: Sampling and summarizing transmission trees with multi-strain infections
timeline.description: Labels internal nodes in phylogenetic tree; weak bottleneck; no explicit transmission model.

timeline.fullTitle: Bayesian reconstruction of transmission trees from genetic sequences and uncertain infection times
timeline.description: Reconstructs phylogenetic tree from transmission tree; Jukes-Cantor model; all cases observed and sampled.
timeline.journal: Statistical Applications in Genetics and Molecular Biology

timeline.fullTitle: Explosive nosocomial outbreak of SARS-CoV-2 in a rehabilitation clinic: the limits of genomics for outbreak reconstruction
timeline.description: Bayesian framework combining genomic and epidemiological data using outbreaker2 to reconstruct transmission trees in a nosocomial SARS-CoV-2 outbreak; assesses limits of genomics for outbreak forensics.

timeline.method: Within-hospital transmission across two pandemic waves
timeline.fullTitle: Characterising within-hospital SARS-CoV-2 transmission events using epidemiological and viral genomic data across two pandemic waves
timeline.description: Combines viral genomic and epidemiological data from 2,181 participants across two pandemic waves at a UK NHS Trust using Bayesian transmission reconstruction; reveals a shift from staff-to-staff to patient-to-patient transmissions between waves, and finds that hospital-onset cases drove most onward transmission.

timeline.fullTitle: Reconstruction of transmission chains of SARS-CoV-2 amidst multiple outbreaks in a geriatric acute-care hospital: a combined retrospective epidemiological and genomic study
timeline.description: Combined retrospective epidemiological and genomic study using outbreaker2 to reconstruct transmission chains of SARS-CoV-2 amidst multiple outbreaks in a geriatric acute-care hospital.

timeline.fullTitle: Bayesian reconstruction of SARS-CoV-2 transmissions highlights substantial proportion of negative serial intervals
timeline.description: Uses a Bayesian framework to infer transmission pairs by exploring all compatible transmission trees based on symptom dates, incorporating a wide range of incubation period and generation time distributions; derives serial intervals from reconstructed pairs, stratified by variants, to account for negative serial intervals.

timeline.fullTitle: Sorting out assortativity: When can we assess the contributions of different population groups to epidemic transmission?
timeline.description: A framework to estimate group transmission assortativity from transmission chain data, quantifying the extent of within-group vs. between-group transmissions while accounting for group sizes and depletion of susceptibles; implemented in an R package.

timeline.fullTitle: A statistical framework for comparing epidemic forests
timeline.description: A statistical framework implemented in the R package mixtree to compare epidemic forests (collections of plausible transmission trees) using chi-square test and PERMANOVA for detecting differences in transmission dynamics.

founder.name: Dr Cyril Geismar
founder.bio: Postdoctoral research fellow. PhD in mathematical modelling of infectious diseases at Imperial College London, focused on SARS-CoV-2 outbreak forensics. Executive board member and developer for the R Epidemics Consortium. Teaches outbreak analytics at Emory University and LSHTM.

advisors.name: Dr Anne Cori
advisors.bio: Associate Professor specialising in real-time outbreak analysis and epidemiological parameters. Lead author of EpiEstim and co-author of outbreaker. Develops statistical methods for outbreak forensics and rapid transmissibility assessment.

advisors.name: Dr Thibaut Jombart
advisors.bio: Associate Professor specialising in outbreak response analytics, biostatistics, population genetics, and R programming. Lead author of outbreaker and founder of the R Epidemics Consortium. Field experience in Ebola deployments in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

title: Next Steps
roadmap.intro: We are seeking funding to validate and deploy NosoTrack in two stages.

phases.title: Simulation Study
phases.desc:
Conduct simulation studies under realistic operational constraints to determine the conditions under which NosoTrack improves outbreak control.
This phase will assess NosoTrack's effectiveness across pathogens, hospital settings, and levels of data availability.

phases.title: Pilot Study
phases.desc:
Deploy the platform in a 1–2 year pilot, integrating EHR and Bluetooth-enabled contact tracing in a live hospital environment.
This phase will generate real-world evidence on reduced infections, cost savings, and improved hospital capacity management.
